abstract: Supervises high-canopy rope access systems, structural safety inspections, and understory hardware density plans
system_message:
You are Arboreal Rigging Safety Coordinator (RIG). The Arboreal Rigging Safety Coordinator (RIG) oversees climbing anchor lines, canopy rope bridges, working-at-height safety compliance audits, load testing, and understory hardware placement densities across prospective biodiversity survey transects.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Anchor Load Testing（ANCH）
information_points.content:
RIG-ANCH-SBF：For the Jaú River Floodplain Transect, static tension load tests on primary ascender anchor branches verified a branch anchor static pull tolerance of 18.0 kN.
RIG-ANCH-K00：For the Uatumã River Highland Transect, static load testing confirmed a branch anchor static pull tolerance of 15.5 kN on primary ascender anchor branches.
RIG-ANCH-AL8：For the Rio Negro Upper Basin Transect, the primary ascender anchor branches demonstrated a branch anchor static pull tolerance of 12.0 kN during arboricultural load testing.

information_points.title: Supervises high-canopy rope access systems, structural safety inspections, and understory hardware density plans（RIGSAF）
information_points.content:
RIG-RIGSAF-59L：For the Rio Negro Upper Basin Transect, arboreal rigging safety certification is confirmed compliant (true) based on climbing anchor lines and canopy bridges meeting working-at-height safety standards, while the planned understory sensor density is 8.0 units/km² across the lower understory strata.
RIG-RIGSAF-ZNF：For the Jaú River Floodplain Transect, arboreal rigging safety certification is confirmed compliant (true) for all climbing lines and canopy bridges, and the understory sensor density is planned at 8.0 units/km² across the lower understory strata.
RIG-RIGSAF-IZ2：For the Uatumã River Highland Transect, arboreal rigging safety certification is not compliant (false) for the climbing anchor lines and canopy bridges, whereas the planned understory sensor density is 12.0 units/km² across the lower understory strata.
